label: COMPETE
prompt: Competitive/pattern research from your knowledge, for a multi-tenant SaaS funnel/CRM web app (a GoHighLevel / ClickFunnels-class competitor) that also wants an AI chat feature. Answer two questions with concrete industry patterns. (1) USER LOGIN + CONNECTORS: How do funnel/CRM SaaS platforms typically implement (a) user social sign-in with Google/Facebook and (b) per-user PLATFORM CONNECTORS to Google/Meta/Instagram/Threads for pulling posts/insights/messages/ads data? Cover the common architecture (hosted OAuth callback, server-side encrypted token store, per-tenant isolation), and the well-known app-review / business-verification gotchas for Meta and Google in production. (2) AI CHAT MODEL STRATEGY: Compare (A) a BUILT-IN model where the SaaS eats inference cost by routing all users through one server-side key to a cheap model (e.g. DeepSeek/​open-weight), vs (B) BRING-YOUR-OWN subscription/API-key where each user connects their own Claude/OpenAI account. Cover: user friction for non-technical users, unit economics, ToS/legal risk of proxying or reselling a PERSONAL AI subscription to third parties, security, and which model real AI SaaS products actually pick as default. Output concise, high-signal structured markdown with headings and short tables. State confidence and flag anything you're unsure of.

label: RISK
prompt: Security risk enumeration for a multi-tenant SaaS web app. Context: the app is adding (1) USER sign-in via 'Login with Google/Facebook' (Supabase GoTrue), (2) per-user OAuth CONNECTORS to Google/Meta/Instagram/Threads to pull data, with tokens stored SERVER-SIDE in Postgres. It is ALSO considering embedding a CLI coding-agent (which holds the OPERATOR's own personal Anthropic/Cursor OAuth tokens) as the in-app chat, potentially shared across all users. Enumerate the TOP security failure modes and edge cases, ranked by severity (Critical/High/Medium), each with a one-line concrete mitigation. Cover at minimum: OAuth redirect-URI manipulation/open-redirect, missing state/CSRF on the callback, authorization-code interception (PKCE), token storage-at-rest & leakage, refresh-token rotation & reuse detection, multi-tenant data isolation / RLS bypass, the SHARED-CLI-CREDENTIAL hazard (one operator subscription serving many tenants — ToS + blast radius + isolation), session/cookie security (httpOnly/Secure/SameSite), and provider app-review/permission over-scoping. Output a single ranked markdown table: Risk | Severity | Why | Mitigation. Concise.
